frontmatter.title: Reducing no-shows at a small dental clinic

problems.statement: I lose clinical capacity and income when booked patients do not attend.
problems.who: Clinic owner, two dentists, and hygienist
problems.evidence: Owner reports approximately one no-show in every eight booked appointments and material financial loss; conversation dated 2026-10-01.

problems.statement: I may miss a visit when appointment details do not reach me or changing the booking is difficult.
problems.who: Patient or person arranging a patient's appointment
problems.evidence: Hypothesis informed by the reminder research and outpatient guidance linked in section 1; not established in this clinic.

problems.statement: I may struggle to attend when cost uncertainty, anxiety, transport, caring duties, or work commitments remain unresolved.
problems.who: Patient with practical or emotional barriers to attendance
problems.evidence: Candidate barriers for local investigation; the owner has not supplied patients' reasons for missing appointments.

problems.statement: I may be unable to refill a released appointment when notice is short or no suitable replacement patient is ready.
problems.who: Person responsible for the clinic's bookings
problems.evidence: Operational hypothesis arising from the reported empty appointments; current cancellation handling and refill performance are unknown.

ideas.idea: Offer reminders through the patient's preferred available channel, with a simple confirmation or change route; trial reminders roughly 72 and 24 hours before the visit, adjusted to the existing cancellation window and staffed response times.

Make a small, prioritized callback list for failed reminders, patients requesting phone contact, and unresolved confirmations, giving attention to long appointments; resolve attendance barriers without treating silence as cancellation.
Maintain an opt-in short-notice list with availability and appointment requirements, then offer released slots to compatible patients and explicitly confirm each replacement booking.
At booking, let the patient choose a workable time, verify contact details and preferences, and give a calendar entry or paper appointment card including the expected visit duration and location.

After a missed appointment, offer a supportive rebooking contact and optionally record a simple reason category so repeated barriers can be addressed; leave the reason unknown when the patient does not explain.
For appointments where cost may be unclear, provide the available estimate and explain what could change it before the visit, with a route to discuss the clinic's existing payment options.
Offer a brief preparation contact when patients identify anxiety or access needs, covering what to expect, practical arrival information, and suitable support agreed with the clinical team.
Test offering suitable patients earlier released appointments and a small amount of near-term booking capacity if long booking lead times are associated with missed visits.
If work or caring conflicts dominate, trial one adjusted clinic session with adequate staffing and patient demand before considering a permanent change to opening hours.

Consider a deposit credited toward selected long elective visits, with clear cancellation terms and appropriate exceptions, only after assessing access effects and the applicable local and payer requirements.
Consider buying a predictive no-show or advanced scheduling system if simple reminder and callback processes leave a material, demonstrable gap that justifies integration and ongoing costs.
Routinely double-book selected slots to compensate for expected no-shows.

assumptions.statement: We believe that avoidable communication or appointment-change friction explains a meaningful share of this clinic's missed visits.
assumptions.validation: Audit existing reminder and outcome records, then compare failure categories and attendance during the pilot; record patient explanations only when volunteered or obtained through appropriate routine follow-up.

assumptions.statement: We believe that the current scheduling and communication tools can support reliable reminders and a monitored change route at modest cost.
assumptions.validation: Inspect available settings and costs, test staff appointments end to end, and verify delivery reporting, reply ownership, and cancellation acknowledgment before live use.

assumptions.statement: We believe that the person handling bookings can sustain selective callbacks and opening management within an acceptable time budget.
assumptions.validation: Record daily minutes during the trial and compare them with the clinic's actual staffing capacity and recovered contribution.

assumptions.statement: We believe that enough patients want earlier clinically suitable appointments to make a short-notice list useful.
assumptions.validation: Track opt-ins, compatible offers, acceptances, actual attendance, and what happens to any later slots released by those patients.

assumptions.statement: We believe that identifying cost, anxiety, or practical access barriers will reveal useful additions beyond reminders.
assumptions.validation: Review optional reason categories and patient feedback over the pilot, keeping unexplained absences unknown and avoiding conclusions from small groups.

assumptions.statement: We believe that the reported 12.5 percent rate can be reproduced from appointment records and provides a useful starting baseline.
assumptions.validation: Recalculate four to eight weeks of counts with a documented denominator, separate cancellations from no-shows, and inspect weekly and appointment-type variation.

assumptions.statement: We believe that most patients can be reached through at least one available communication channel that fits their preferences and access needs.
assumptions.validation: Check contact accuracy, delivery failures, preferred channels, and feedback; compare reach and attendance for text and non-text routes without withdrawing existing support.

assumptions.statement: We believe that some additional attended appointments will produce net financial benefit after extra costs and any displacement of later visits.
assumptions.validation: Reconcile attended appointment and slot records with collections, variable treatment costs, staff time, and tool costs; distinguish visits moved earlier from net additional completed care.
